![kody code-review](https://img.shields.io/badge/kody-code--review-312B4B?labelColor=C9BBF2) ![Bug](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bug-B71C1C) ![high](https://img.shields.io/badge/severity_level-high-6B6B92)


**includeChangeRequests true despite unaddressed PR-level findings**

A run whose only output was PR-level findings is held as not clean, yet `includeChangeRequests` still dismisses Kody's earlier CHANGES_REQUESTED review while those findings remain unaddressed. Add `(context.prLevelCommentResults?.length ?? 0) === 0` to the predicate so dismissal follows the same cleanliness rule as `reviewClean` in `decide-pr-approval.stage.ts`.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/code-review/pipeline/stages/finish-process-review.stage.ts, lines 76-82:

includeChangeRequests true despite unaddressed PR-level findings

`includeChangeRequests` treats the review as having no findings when `lineComments` is empty, but the pipeline's own `reviewClean` definition (decide-pr-approval.stage.ts:216-223) also requires `prLevelCommentResults` to be empty, so a run whose only output was PR-level findings reaches this branch as a `hold` ('The review is not clean.') yet still gets `includeChangeRequests: true`. That dismisses Kody's earlier CHANGES_REQUESTED review while the current review's PR-level findings remain unaddressed and the same stage's `approvePullRequest` call counts those PR-level results as findings (lines 191-194). Add `(context.prLevelCommentResults?.length ?? 0) === 0` to the predicate so dismissal only happens for a review that is clean by the same definition used to decide the hold.
````

</details>


<sub>Talk to Kody by mentioning @kody</sub>


<sub>Was this suggestion helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to help Kody learn from this interaction.</sub>

<!-- kody-codereview -->​
​

## Code Review Completed! 🔥

The code review was successfully completed based on your current configurations.



<details>
<summary>Kody Guide: Usage and Configuration</summary>

<details>
<summary>Interacting with Kody</summary>

- **Request a Review:** Ask Kody to review your PR manually by adding a comment with the \`@kody start-review\` command at the root of your PR.

- **Provide Feedback:** Help Kody learn and improve by reacting to its comments with a 👍 for helpful suggestions or a 👎 if improvements are needed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Providing Context (Files & MCPs)</summary>

Add these hints in your PR description (or a comment) to unlock deeper checks:

- **Ticket / Acceptance Criteria:** \`Refs: ABC-123\` (Linear/Jira/Asana/ClickUp/Trello) or a direct ticket link.
- **Bugfix Validation:** a Sentry/Datadog/Bugsnag event link (or paste the stack trace/error message).
- **Endpoint Risk:** mention the route (e.g., \`POST /api/payments\`) or controller/action name.
- **Attach a repo file as context:** use an explicit marker like \`@file:docs/guide.mdx#L10-L50\` (replace with your real path).
- **API Contract Docs:** include \`@file:openapi.yaml\` or \`@file:swagger.json\` when changing routes/schemas.
- **Definition of Done / Standards:** include \`@file:DOD.md\` or \`@file:CONTRIBUTING.md\` if your repo has them.
- **Design System Source of Truth:** include \`@file:ui/index.ts\` (replace with your DS entrypoint path).
- **Feature Flags:** include the flag key/name and \`@file:flags.ts\` / \`@file:config.json\` (and optionally the PostHog flag name).
- **Edge/CDN Rules:** link the Cloudflare rule/zone or describe the intended redirect/header behavior.
- **Attach an MCP tool output:** use \`@mcp<provider|tool>\` (replace with an installed MCP provider + tool, e.g., \`@mcp<sentry|events.search>\`).

</details>

**Kody Code Review** — 1 suggested fix.
Paste the prompt below to your agent and all review fixed at once!

<details>
<summary>🛠️ Open Agent Prompt</summary>

```
A code review identified the following issues in this pull request.
Each section describes what was found and includes a reference implementation where available.

Files involved:
- libs/code-review/pipeline/stages/finish-process-review.stage.ts:82

---

### [1/1] libs/code-review/pipeline/stages/finish-process-review.stage.ts:82
Issue identified during code review:
includeChangeRequests true despite unaddressed PR-level findings

`includeChangeRequests` treats the review as having no findings when `lineComments` is empty, but the pipeline's own `reviewClean` definition (decide-pr-approval.stage.ts:216-223) also requires `prLevelCommentResults` to be empty, so a run whose only output was PR-level findings reaches this branch as a `hold` ('The review is not clean.') yet still gets `includeChangeRequests: true`. That dismisses Kody's earlier CHANGES_REQUESTED review while the current review's PR-level findings remain unaddressed and the same stage's `approvePullRequest` call counts those PR-level results as findings (lines 191-194). Add `(context.prLevelCommentResults?.length ?? 0) === 0` to the predicate so dismissal only happens for a review that is clean by the same definition used to decide the hold.

---

Review each issue in context, use the reference implementations as guidance, and apply fixes that are consistent with the surrounding codebase.
```

</details>

**[Access your configuration settings here.](https://app.kodus.io/settings/code-review/global/general)**

</details>

Kody's assessment:
> The change alters PR gating: Kody now dismisses its own CHANGES_REQUESTED review on a clean hold, unblocking merges. The guard (no line comments, no failures) may not mirror all approval-path safeguards (e.g., custom-agent-only runs), and the diff shows only the type added in codeManagement.service, so forwarding of includeChangeRequests to the GitHub adapter is unverified. Tests cover stage and adapter separately, not the end-to-end path, and this area has high recent bug-fix churn.
